channel.title: AI Tool Lab - AI News
channel.description: Daily AI news briefs with editorial analysis.

item.title: Meta details LLM pipeline behind Facebook Your Algorithm ranking
item.description: Meta detailed the engineering behind Your Algorithm, which lets Facebook users type interests for Feed and Reels. Each typed interest drives four retrieval sources, and a fine-tuned LLM reranker outputs only items to remove, which Meta says beat a general-purpose model on speed and reliability. The system passed no user metrics.

item.title: Anthropic lets users install Claude Artifacts as macOS and Windows apps
item.description: Anthropic began beta-testing installation of Claude Artifacts as macOS and Windows apps, requiring the latest Claude desktop client. Installed apps can call OS APIs, connectors and Claude itself to add menu bar items, transparent windows and notifications. A free account is enough, and Apple Developer accounts can build standalone apps.

item.title: Jensen Huang apologizes to Nvidia staff, denies Trump helped reinstate him
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologized to staff in his first all-hands since returning, calling claims that Trump directly secured his reinstatement completely untrue. He said politics played no role and acknowledged violating the company's code of conduct, adding that he is in therapy daily. Huang resigned on November 12 and was reinstated Monday.

item.title: AI agents generate 450% more network traffic than human workers
item.description: A report sponsored by Tata Communications says tasks run by AI agents generate an estimated 450 percent more network traffic than the same tasks done by people. As inference moves on-premises for lower latency, as few as half of enterprises believe their networks can handle AI's bandwidth demands. The report points to network-as-a-service and AI observability as responses.

item.title: GPT-6 models design proteins using reasoning and code, study reports
item.description: OpenAI reported that GPT-6 models can design protein structures and sequences using reasoning and code, without specialized biology models. In wet-lab tests, 35 of 322 designed minibinders bound across five targets, a 10.9 percent hit rate. On MotifBench the models scored 43.7 percent versus 27.8 percent for specialized approaches.

item.title: DeepMind agent teams cut quantum algorithm costs using Lean proofs
item.description: DeepMind used teams of Gemini 4 agents to optimize quantum algorithms, proving each circuit correct with the Lean theorem prover and open-sourcing the library. For inertial confinement fusion, agents cut computing cost 11.8-fold and memory from 5,650 to 4,338 error-corrected qubits. They also found a 290-fold speedup for arcsin and 2.5-fold for Cytochrome P450 simulations.

item.title: Honeypot Research Exposes Data-Theft Chain Among AI Inference Providers
item.description: Dragos' 2 million honeypot requests found at least 3 providers compromised and hundreds of AWS keys stolen and used; OpenRouter removed 3 and revoked ZDR eligibility for 125 endpoints.

item.title: Riemann Hypothesis Proof Formally Certified by Lean Community
item.description: The Lean and Mathlib communities issued a statement confirming that mathematician Alpöge’s proof of the Riemann Hypothesis has passed verification: about 17 million lines of code, dozens of people independently reproduced consistent results, and certification was obtained within 24 hours.

item.title: AA Evaluation: GPT-6.2 More Concise but Less Transparent
item.description: AA personality benchmark: both GPT-6.2 models give answers 34–40% shorter, admitting uncertainty falls to 24 and 51, and transparency at 41 and 57 trails Claude's 81 and 90.

item.title: FT investigation reveals Megaspeed chip transshipment network
item.description: An FT investigation alleges that some Nvidia chips at Megaspeed were suspected of being transshipped to China: its Malaysian subsidiary declared about $4.6 billion in imports from Aivres over one year, implicating Hu Xiaowei and Century Huatong, both subject to US and UK sanctions.

item.title: Qwen4 Max Fixes a Tornado Framework Bug in a Single Call
item.description: Alibaba's flagship model landed on the Together inference platform with 1M context. Loading the entire Tornado repository - 650K tokens across 344 files - it produced a passing patch in 72 seconds for $0.69.

item.title: OpenAI Ships GPT-Live-1.1 Voice Model on the API
item.description: The full-duplex voice model defaults to 128K context and is exclusive to OpenAI's cloud. A new standby idle billing mode costs $0.02/minute - 60% below the active rate of $0.05.

item.title: Anthropic Mathematician Claims Claude Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis
item.description: Mathematician Alpöge says the claimed proof also covers the generalized Riemann hypothesis, published as 14 Lean packages spanning over 250,000 printed pages. Hours later, Stanford released a competing human-only draft by mathematician Masullo.

item.title: Claude Code Launches Experimental Code Mode
item.description: Claude Code's new Code Mode has the model write JavaScript to complete multi-step tool calls in one pass, supporting parallel execution and output filtering. The experimental feature is off by default; early tests report 22-23% lower bills and up to 77% token reduction.

item.title: Nasdaq 100 Suffers Worst Week Since the Pandemic: Down 10.4%
item.description: The Nasdaq 100 fell 5.6% on Friday, closing the week down 10.4% - a 20% retreat from October highs that puts the index in bear-market territory. Nvidia plummeted 14% on Friday amid reported SEC scrutiny of its accounting practices.

item.title: MiniMax MIM Achieves First Practical Breaks on Multiple NIST Candidates
item.description: MiniMax's MIM delivered the first practical cryptanalysis breaks on several NIST candidate algorithms, solving 55 previously unsolved McEliece challenge instances - up to a 43,000x speedup over prior records.

item.title: OpenHands Hands CVE Remediation to an Agent Pipeline
item.description: October set a record with 17,000 new CVEs. OpenHands now routes most fixes through agents: mirrors cut fixable criticals from 87 to 5 and highs from 1,997 to 188.

item.title: Anthropic Slides 9% on Day Two, Nears $83 IPO Price
item.description: Shares closed at $88.30 on the second trading day, down 9%, with the Nasdaq now down 5% year-to-date. Asian stocks had their worst week since 2020; SoftBank fell 14.5% in a day and Micron 12%.

item.title: METR Update: AI Task Time Horizon Doubles Every 3.6 Months
item.description: Covering 15 models through GPT-6 Astra and Opus 5.5, the merged TH1.1+TH2 suite shows a 3.61-month doubling cycle; the TH2 verifiable subset doubles in just 1.65 months.

item.title: Thinking Machines Lab Releases Laptop-Runnable Inkling 2 Mini
item.description: A recurrent transformer whose middle 12 layers run 3 times per token. MoE total parameters 26.4B with 3.4B active, around 20GB - it runs on a 32GB Mac.

item.title: Runway's Software Factory: Agents Now Land 38% of Merged PRs
item.description: Runway reports agents drove 38% of merged PRs in October - up from 0.1% in June - with monthly merges going from 2 to over 3,000, and first-approval wait times down from 2.3 hours to 5 minutes.

item.title: Browser Use 1.0: 24 Tools Consolidated Into One
item.description: Browser Use 1.0 replaces 24 discrete action tools with a single Python REPL plus CDP. Same-model benchmark scores rose 14-33 points while costs fell to between 1/2.7 and 1/5.2 of previous levels.

item.title: Amodei Pledges Not to Bow to Commercial or Political Pressure
item.description: In his IPO-day remarks, Amodei committed to slowing AI training and deployment whenever necessary until systems are provably safe and under human control, regardless of commercial or political pressure - saying going public strengthens that resolve.

item.title: Stanford Benchmark Tracks AI-Written Court Filings
item.description: Stanford's PhantomDocket benchmark calibrates detectors using an AI-hallucination corpus: in 2026, 38% of Santa Clara County complaints showed AI traces, with self-represented filers rising from 19% to 72%.

item.title: Google Opens Genie 4 World Model API
item.description: Google opened Genie 4 to developers: text- or image-generated interactive 720p 24fps worlds with 48kHz stereo audio and keyboard control, at about $6.05/minute with 120-second session limits.

item.title: Anthropic Rises 17% on Debut, Raises $81.3B in Largest IPO Ever
item.description: Anthropic's $81.34 billion raise tops SpaceX as the largest IPO in history, nearly 7x oversubscribed. Priced at $83, the stock opened up 34% and closed with a $1.27 trillion market cap.

item.title: Perplexity Brain Writes Its Own Personal Skills
item.description: The Perplexity Brain agent automatically writes and updates personal skills from conversation history. In an 8-week randomized test, 72.9% of users gained new skills and tool-call failures dropped 11% at unchanged cost.

item.title: OpenAI Uses Codex to Auto-Investigate Performance Regressions
item.description: OpenAI's Performance Factory has Codex agents investigate and fix ChatGPT performance regressions: 1,700+ investigations and 600+ root causes over three months, with 70% spot-check accuracy.

item.title: Gemini for Mac Adds Computer Control
item.description: Google shipped computer use for Gemini on Mac: multi-step tasks across desktop apps, local files and the web, running in background windows without occupying the cursor. Rolling out first to US subscribers.

item.title: DeepMind Releases Gemini 4 Neon
item.description: Google DeepMind releases Gemini 4 Neon: intelligence index 61 points, ranking 3rd; first on the coding agent index; cost per task 32% lower than Carbon.
